items.title: Complex odors prove easier to map than expected with machine learning
items.excerpt: Monell Chemical Senses Center researchers built machine learning models that distinguish scents and map how they relate to one another. The work points toward "digital olfaction" — representing smell mathematically the way color and sound were digitized — with uses in diagnostics and product development.

items.title: Seeing the unseen: A new tool visualizes hidden structures in complex biological data
items.excerpt: University of Basel researchers released Bonsai, which renders high-dimensional single-cell data as branching trees instead of flat 2D maps, preserving true distances between cells. The tool surfaced a previously unknown natural killer cell subtype in human blood.

items.title: AI screens 100,000+ membrane combinations, predicting carbon capture performance within seconds
items.excerpt: A Koç University team combined molecular simulation with machine learning to evaluate more than 104,000 mixed-matrix membrane combinations for carbon capture. The framework predicts a candidate's performance in seconds at roughly 10–15% error, collapsing a screening job that would take years in the lab.

items.title: AI-designed "intrabodies" could unlock new treatments for Alzheimer's, Parkinson's and MND
items.excerpt: University of Essex researchers used AI to redesign ordinary antibodies into tiny fragments that stay stable and functional inside living human cells, targeting disease proteins that conventional antibodies can't reach. Published in Nature Communications, the redesigned molecules will be released freely to other labs.

items.title: We still don't know how people are really using AI
items.excerpt: A new independent research project, the AI Observatory, aggregates consented real conversations with Claude and Gemini to build a public picture of AI use. It found nearly half of conversations are non-work — health, relationships, sensitive topics — categories that vendor usage reports largely omit.

items.title: No, Anthropic's AI didn't just solve math's hardest problem
items.excerpt: Claude helped sharpen a result about the distribution of prime numbers that sits adjacent to the Riemann hypothesis — real, checkable progress, but not the $1-million problem itself. The piece is a case study in how AI math claims get inflated between the preprint and the headline.

items.title: OpenAI funds research to try to stop AI from being used to make bioweapons
items.excerpt: OpenAI awarded grants to 14 organizations, including the Nuclear Threat Initiative, to build cross-border systems for sharing biosecurity threat information about AI-enabled biology. It's an admission that model capability in the life sciences has outrun the safeguards around it.

items.title: How generative AI is reshaping creativity, and what it means for artists
items.excerpt: Astrophysicist and folklorist Moiya McTier traces humanity's creative history through the Greek muses and asks what generative AI does to authorship. The conversation is about what creative practice is for, not just what tools can produce.

items.title: AI has created a shadow medical system
items.excerpt: More than 40 million Americans ask ChatGPT a health question every day, almost entirely outside clinical settings. Paired with direct-to-consumer labs and AI-generated prescriptions, that has quietly assembled a parallel care system with no physician oversight or accountability.

items.title: I'm a pediatrician. AI chatbots are grooming my patients
items.excerpt: A pediatrician documents chatbot interactions with minors that follow grooming patterns, including AI systems drawing patients into sexual conversation. He argues these products generate the harmful content rather than merely host it, so product liability should apply.

items.title: Quantum X Labs Tests AI Quantum Error Decoder on Google Hardware Dataset
items.excerpt: Quantum X Labs reported that its AI-driven surface-code decoder improved accuracy on Google's public real-hardware dataset while having been trained purely on synthetic data. Transferring from simulation to physical qubits without hardware-specific retraining is the hard part of the problem.

items.title: From Models to Agents: The Next Phase of AI Adoption in Molecular Discovery
items.excerpt: Biotech is moving past single predictive models toward agentic systems that chain structure prediction, literature reading and docking into one workflow. NYB.AI's Vecura platform is the worked example, with the argument that agents close the gap between generating an insight and acting on it.

items.title: AI could offer a shortcut for designing more efficient airplane wings
items.excerpt: Researchers report a machine learning approach that substitutes for expensive fluid-dynamics simulation in aerodynamic shape optimization, cutting the cost of exploring wing geometries. Published time taken from New Scientist's own RSS pubDate (the site blocks our fetcher).

items.title: AI firms are watermarking generated text – here's why it won't work
items.excerpt: AI companies are shipping statistical watermarks into generated text, but the technique degrades under paraphrase, translation and light editing. Provenance for written work is turning out to be far harder than for images. Published time from New Scientist RSS pubDate.

items.title: Elon Musk and Sam Altman claim we've reached the AI singularity. But how would we even know that happened?
items.excerpt: Live Science asks what measurable evidence a "singularity" claim would actually require, and finds the definitions used by industry leaders are unfalsifiable. A useful counterweight to capability rhetoric, grounded in how scientists set thresholds. Published time from Live Science RSS pubDate.
